intro: Everything open on Titan Reliquary, as of build BUILD, ordered by what matters most now: turning the ledger's guesses into checked facts and the research loop that does it, then safety, then the new app (on hold while Grok upgrades the themes), motion and polish. Designed for your own experience (Oct 20: no separate Dad mode). Every item says what it needs first. Tick what you want, press Copy my picks and paste the line back to me. Numbers never change between versions; new items are marked new. The numbers at the top, the questions and the AI cards are read live from the data.

sotu.one: the most trustworthy record of a personal coin collection, researched by a team of AIs that check each other. Every fact shows where it came from, which AI or person said it, who checked it and how sure we are, and you confirm what only the coin can answer with one tap. Nobody does this for a private collection.
strong: A research system that runs itself.

Every gap in the data is homework: the loop hands each AI the jobs it is best at, never its own facts to check, files every disagreement instead of overwriting, and measures each AI by how often its facts turn out wrong. Since Oct 20 the never-checked ledger facts go first, read blind from the photos, and about 900 items are out to Grok, Muse and Gemini.

Every fact has a certainty label, a history and now a link to its exact source; “Checked” means two independent sources agree. The change history is sealed (a correction is a new line, never an edit), and every photo is fingerprinted against its original.
One pipeline, one master, tested on every update.

Any AI drops a change file; one script checks it, merges it and rebuilds the site. 53 pipeline tests, 19 research-loop tests, a 38-point phone + desktop smoke test and a GitHub integrity check run on every update; a monthly restore drill rebuilds the whole site from the backup.
Daily prices, live-site check, smoke and integrity checks and a daily backup zip run on GitHub; Health warns when any fails.

The whole collection opens as a spreadsheet (coins, album holes, lots, every source) and as one JSON file, a printable inventory exists, and a recovery card says how to rebuild everything from the daily backup.
holding: A third of the facts are still the old ledger's word.

Of 3,402 facts on screen, 1,781 are cited or confirmed (52.4 %), 474 of them Checked by two sources; 1,106 still come from the original ledger unchecked and 371 are AI readings without an exact source. The ledger's year, mint and face value on photographed coins are now first in line (#125).
The loop needs me to turn it.
AIs drop files in Drive; nothing merges until a session opens. The autonomous intake (#92) that removes this is built and tested; it switches on with your one-time install (about 10 minutes).
The interface is behind the system, and you said so.

Judged blind on Oct 16, every badge and theme pair came back "both weak". Grok is upgrading the themes on main now; Titan v3 (#119-#121) waits until that pass is done, and is built for your own experience.
79 pieces have no photo, most have only one side, none have pro photos. The Scan page makes each one a few taps; Phase 2 cannot start before them.
Nothing from Gemini since Oct 16; its 15 assignments include the 12 disagreements only a third reader can settle. Claude settles the clear ones meanwhile.
next: Send Grok, Muse and Gemini to their WORK QUEUE docs (all updated today, with bigger batches). The one-time install for #92 still saves the most: their files then merge every hour without a chat.
79 pieces have no photo (C293 and C300 among them); Scan a coin names and sends each one. That and the 31 unread mint marks are all that stands between Phase 1 and 100 %.
And decide #127 (Grok's direct pushes, the AIs' Drive reach) when you have a minute.

chains: The loop running without a chat (#92)
needs your one-time install (one Apps Script project, two GitHub secrets; about 10 minutes) ← nothing else: the bridge, the loop, the gates and the tests are built
needs serial numbers (#5) ← Phase 1 at 100 % (now 216 of 306: 79 photos and 31 mint marks missing) ← the ledger checked against the photos (#125) + the varieties checklist (#126)
needs Muse's locked test (due on its page) and Gemini's when it is back ← Grok's is in: 76 % right, 3.0 % invented
Reading a coin inside the app (#65 next step)
needs the winner of #19 ← a key kept outside the public site (#92's machinery)
needs Gemini to answer its arbitration homework (12 open, on its page; nothing from Gemini since Oct 16) ← Claude settles the clear ones meanwhile (37 on Oct 20)
Real collector values for every coin (#62)
needs Grok's appraisal homework (running) + your free Numista API key (the weekly price job); album costs (#107) use the same prices
Motion and the gold dust in the app (#63)
needs design direction (#30) + app split (#32) + your phone speed number (#25) + your picks from the Motion Lab (#56)
you: Switch on the autonomous intake + Drive backup (once, about 10 minutes):

follow docs/INTAKE_BRIDGE.md (github.com/jpavia10/titan-reliquary-preview/blob/main/docs/INTAKE_BRIDGE.md): one Apps Script project and two GitHub secrets. Then the AIs' files merge by themselves every hour and Drive gets a daily backup (#92, #93, #103). Never paste the URL or the key in a chat; tell me “the bridge is installed” and I run the first check.
Print the recovery card:
Drive → Titan Reliquary → 'RECOVERY CARD (print this, keep it in the safe)'; write your GitHub and Google recovery codes on it by hand (#105).
Two write paths to narrow, your call:
Grok's direct pushes to main, and the AIs' reach into your whole Drive (#127).
No rush on the coin questions:
they can wait for the pro-photo session. When you do answer some, press Send to Claude on the Questions page; it then shows Received when they are in (#118).
Photograph the missing coins with Scan a coin
(Hall footer, or Lab → Shoot list → Scan with the camera): it checks each photo, names it and sends it to Drive STAGING. Unlocks Phase 1 at 100 %.
Get a free Numista API key

(numista.com → your account → API) and add it in GitHub: the repository → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New secret, name NUMISTA_API_KEY. The weekly price job then fills in collector values (#62). Never paste the key in a chat.
Measure your phone's speed:
Health → Measure speed → Add this speed report to my answers file, then send the answers file (#25).
Decide who gets which inventory copy:
Health → Printable inventory (with values for the insurer, without for the family) (#64).
Decide: does every coin need both sides photographed?
Or can the common side of common coins be shared from one good photo? It sets the size of the “other side” batch (194 coins) and #61.
Opening: every launch plays the Grok film, then the theme's motion,
and picking a theme plays its motion too; 9 new Grok films joined the rotation on Oct 14. Change it in Scene Studio → Settings → Opening (#112).
Re-upload 4 photos smaller than 7 MB:
Judge the new designs blind:
when Titan v3 step 1 or The Field v2 is ready I send you a blind-test link; pick A, B or both weak (#119, #122). The older prototypes are at jpavia10.github.io/titan-reliquary-preview/prototypes/v2/.
Try the new theme effects on your phone:
open a few themes (Scene Studio → Themes) and tell me which effects are too strong, too faint or stutter (#114).

1.title: Process new drops from Grok and Muse
1.desc: Muse's 3 coins filed as C281 France 1994 5 francs, C282 Yugoslavia 1965 50 para, C283 Germany 2002 10 cent; photos cut; Muse scored 7/10.

2.title: Fix album A006 hole count (80 → 77)
2.desc: Mercury dime album: the 80 was an estimate; your page photos show 77 holes. It is a question in the app, because only you can lower a count.

3.title: Settle the open curation questions
3.desc: 14 questions wait in the app (Hall footer → Questions), plus the “Where did they come from?” section (#77). With the coin in hand each takes seconds. Oct 15: the three about Muse's coins are settled on Muse's readings, as you asked (C302 UK 1922 penny, C303 a second Australia 1983 one cent, C304 Mexico 1981 20 pesos).

4.title: Photo-model bake-off
4.desc: Main 30-coin test: Grok 78 % right, 3.8 % invented (Oct 8); Muse 71 %, 5.3 %, 17 % false confidence; Gemini 85 %, 3.0 % (Oct 12, but it worked from a copy of the repository in Drive, so its catalogue numbers may come from our own records: a weak measure). The test recurs by itself every 6 months.
4.needs: Gemini's locked test when it is back (paused: the Argon release broke its app)

5.title: Plan the serial reassignment
5.desc: New display serials with no scan-order bias, done once. Decide first: should the numbers mean something (grouped by country) or carry no pattern?
5.needs: #57 at 100 % and your East Caribbean code answer (#3)
5.unlocks: #61 (you write the new id on each coin’s back)

6.title: Health screen in the app
6.desc: Shows which build and data version you are seeing, offline cache state, photo coverage, problems found.

7.title: Automatic live-site check after each deploy
7.desc: A GitHub job confirms the live site really serves the new build and data.

8.title: Refresh button says what happened
8.desc: "Updated to tr92" or "Already current", never a silent reload.

9.title: Certainty labels in the coin view
9.desc: Each fact marked Verified, Owner-confirmed, Reference-backed, AI guess or Needs review.

10.title: Coin history in the coin view
10.desc: A short timeline: logged, story added, photo found a mismatch, corrected.

11.title: “Why do we believe this?” per fact
11.desc: Already there since tr93: tap any certainty label in a coin’s view to see who said it, when, the source, and whether it was checked; History shows every change.

12.title: Show value with its uncertainty
12.desc: The Hall headline now reads: about $5.4k = melt $4,383 (firm) plus about $1.0k collector premium (estimate).

13.title: Label album slots as tracked, not catalogued
13.desc: Album counts now say "tracked, not catalogued" in the Hall, Study and Simple view.

14.title: Record which AI, prompt and photo produced each fact
14.desc: So a later correction shows what went wrong and who got it right.

15.title: Keep crop settings with every photo
15.desc: Cheap now and impossible to recover later. Lets us test whether better crops make the AIs read coins better.

16.title: Split the AI scorecard in two
16.desc: "Follows the rules" (today's score) vs "gets coins right" (new, measured).

17.title: Exact sources per fact
17.desc: Catalogue facts from an AI must cite the exact entry (Numista N#…, KM#…, URL, page); a bare "Numista" now rejects the file.

18.title: Keep AI disagreements as records
18.desc: Oct 9 (tr104): every disagreement between two contributors is kept in collection/disagreements.jsonl with both values, both sources, who said what and how it was settled. A check that disagrees is filed there and never overwrites the record; a third reader (or you) settles it, and the loser is counted wrong. The first 7 are the Oct 8 Muse-vs-record conflicts.

19.title: Locked coin test for scoring AIs over time
19.desc: Grok took the 15-coin locked test (Oct 10): 76 % of the core fields right, 47 % of catalogue numbers, 3.0 % invented (2 of 66 values), never wrong when sure; it left 17 of 60 core fields blank rather than guess. This is the reference number for who reads the Phase 2 pro photos. Muse's and Gemini's locked tests are still due.
19.needs: Muse's locked test; Gemini's when it is back

20.title: Track AI cost against facts produced
20.desc: New collaborators/AI_RUNS.md: one line per AI file (events, kept, verified, cost). Costs fill in once AIs report them.

21.title: Sounds for the effect moments
21.desc: Done (tr110): every effect moment has its own short sound (the whale, the press strike, the shooting star, POW, the clay drop, the foil sweep...), at most one every 12 seconds and only while the app is on screen; Scene Studio > Settings has an “Effect moment sounds” switch.

22.title: Tune sound and music from your listening
22.desc: Levels, rain, 3D placement, choir, drums: fix what you report.

23.title: Black Site terminal readability
23.desc: Done (tr109): the Construct's terminal is hidden on narrow screens and drawn at 14 px without glow; its falling code gave way to the new ASCII-art effect, which keeps clear of text.

24.title: Music tempo slider in Scene Studio
24.desc: Tempo slider (70–140 %) in Scene Studio → Sound, remembered between visits.

25.title: Speed budget and phone check
25.desc: Fixed limits are checked on every deploy (first load, page size, time to a real value, longest freeze). Now one tap brings your phone's real numbers: Health → Measure speed → Add this speed report to my answers file.

26.title: Gallery side cards show the coin backs
26.desc: Side cards now show the coin's photo even when only the back was photographed (same rule as the tiles).

27.title: Study "0 of 0" chips
27.desc: No longer happens: every album now has a known slot total.

28.title: Vault narration voice
28.desc: Review the spoken voice in the Vault wing. Grok suggests parking it.

29.title: Make buttons look tappable
29.desc: Some controls do not look clickable.

30.title: Pick the final design direction
30.desc: Combine the three prototypes or ask for new options. This ends the design pause; every visual change waits on it.

31.title: Automatic smoke test of the whole app
31.desc: 23 checks on phone and desktop (every wing, search, coin view, 3D table, offline) run on every deploy.

32.title: Split app.js into modules
32.desc: Steps 1–5 done (tr96–tr105; step 5 = the data layer, js/app-data.js). Next: the theme system and its effects (it shares a global name with the GPU effects, so it moves with a check), then the big wings one at a time, each smoke-tested.

33.title: Schema upgrade tests
33.desc: Prove each data-format upgrade keeps every fact.

34.title: Update the Drive "AI_START_HERE" doc
34.desc: Make the Drive copy match the repo so outside AIs see the current counts and rules.

35.title: Finish the 12 missing splash films
35.desc: Any video AI, max 4 clips per run. Grok and Muse both suggest cutting this until the design is chosen (#30): about $52 bought 2 clips.
35.needs: a video AI with credits, and #30

36.title: Questions for you, answered in the app
36.desc: Questions page in the app (Hall footer → Questions): tap answers, then send them as one file.

37.title: Count the silver already sitting in your albums
37.desc: Your albums hold 1.06 oz of silver (1964 Kennedy, 1966 and 1967 40% halves, two Roosevelt dimes, a Mercury dime, a 1964 quarter), and it is in the silver total.

38.title: Explain the 1.5 oz of bullion silver no record accounts for
38.desc: Solved from Grok's own notes: the 1.5 oz is the silver in your albums, counted from day one. One album was over-estimated (Kennedy A007: the photo shows 3 silver halves, not 6), so silver is now 62.83 oz and the total $28 lower.

39.title: Fix the catalog numbers Muse flagged
39.desc: Oct 6–8: 11 of 12 fixed, Eritrea last (C212 is KM#47, Numista N#2403, 7.8 g, 25 mm; Grok re-checks it in the sweep). The 12th, the C238 portrait name, is a question for you in the app.

40.title: Replace the approximate weights with catalog weights
40.desc: Oct 8 (tr102): every swept type now carries the catalogue weight and size from Numista instead of a range (Jamaica $1 3.65 g, Mexico 5 pesos 3 g, Trinidad 25 cents 3.53 g and more); the few left are in Grok’s round 2.

41.title: Find possible duplicate records
41.desc: One possible double entry: C169 and C275 (both UK 1992 5p). Now a question for you.

42.title: Warn when the spot price is stale
42.desc: The Hall shows the daily price date and warns if it is over 36 h old. Also fixed the daily price job, which failed on Oct 5.

43.title: Owner "confirm" button on each fact
43.desc: Tap any label in a coin's view → "I checked the coin: this is right". It waits in Questions until you send it.

44.title: Certainty chips in the Lab, Study and 3D table
44.desc: Lab and Study already open the same coin view with labels; the 3D table got a "How sure we are" button.

45.title: Tell Grok and Muse about provenance in their feedback docs
45.desc: Grok and Muse feedback docs now carry the provenance and exact-source rules.

46.title: Retire the unused Swiss type record
46.desc: CH.KM.24a has no coins since the split; remove it so the integrity report is clean.

47.title: Read in Muse's own file format automatically
47.desc: A converter now turns Muse's own format into proper change files and lists what to check on the photo, including possible duplicates.

48.title: Re-cite Muse's 26 vague sources
48.desc: Muse has the list (its REJECTED note and queue): each one moves from “AI guess” to “Reference” when Muse resends it with the exact entry. Still pending.

49.title: Warn when a daily job fails
49.desc: Health now has a "Background jobs" section, and the Hall's Health button shows ⚠ when any job failed.

50.title: Process your answers file automatically
50.desc: When you drop answers_owner_*.json in Drive, it becomes records without waiting for a chat. #92 lists it for me but does not merge it on its own: your answers become Verified facts, and any AI with access to the folder could write a file under that name. Two ways: Google Drive added to the daily routine, or an answers file the app signs so #92 can tell it is yours.
50.needs: Drive in the routine (you), or a signed answers file (#92 installed first)

51.title: GitHub job versions before Oct 19
51.desc: Checked GitHub's own warnings: the old actions already run on the new engine. The real Oct 19 change is Ubuntu 26, so the smoke test (which installs a browser) is pinned to Ubuntu 24.04.

52.title: Questions badge for your dad
52.desc: Oct 8 (tr100): the Hall shows “15 questions only the coin can answer” next to the trust number, and the Simple view opens with a big “Answer the questions” button.

53.title: Act on Muse's process audit
53.desc: tr98: the next coin id is now published for every AI; a possible double entry is flagged at intake; files in a made-up format are bounced instead of fixed by Claude; the record of which AI made each fact is required from Oct 21; reshoot naming written down. A bounced file no longer costs probation.

54.title: Shoot list in the right order
54.desc: Oct 8 (tr100): Lab → Shoot list. Photos that settle one of your questions come first, then a research question, then an unread mint mark, then value × doubt, then the oldest. “Start here” shows the top 12; a second batch lists the 194 coins that need their other side, and which side.

55.title: Two AIs read each new coin
55.desc: Oct 9 (tr105): automatic. When an AI reads a new coin from its photo, the year, mint mark and face value go blind to a second AI (it never sees the first reading); agreement makes them “Checked”, a difference becomes a disagreement record. New-coin files are also compared with double_read.py before merging.

56.title: Motion Lab test page
56.desc: Done (tr110): six studies at /motion-lab/: gold dust (Grok), Morph (your second video, rebuilt with your coins: dust sheet, a coin formed from its photo, the burst, light ribbons, blue beams), coin flip with a rim light, a tile growing into the coin view, the Confirm seal (AI guess → Owner verified) and a coin settling into album A026. Still / Calm / Full on each. Oct 14: two more coin-flip studies, 3B by Grok and 3C by Gemini (its coin notes are marked unchecked). Tell me which ones you want in the app (#63).

57.title: Phase 1 finish line
57.desc: Oct 8 (tr100): one bar in the Lab and in Health: 172 of 285 pieces are through Phase 1. The 7 fields are frozen (photo, country, year, denomination, mint mark read from the coin, story, default value); 77 still need a photo and 55 need their mint mark read. The Lab lists exactly what each piece lacks.

58.title: Restore drill
58.desc: Oct 8 (tr100): the backup zip was rebuilt into an empty folder; the master validated, the data came out identical (285 flips, same headline) and the restored site passed all 27 smoke checks on phone and desktop. Runs again on the 3rd of every month. The opening films and sound recordings are left out of the compact backup on purpose (they stay in GitHub).

59.title: One motion setting
59.desc: Oct 8 (tr100): Scene Studio → Sound → Settings → Motion: Full / Calm / Off for everything that moves (effects, the opening film, page movement, the Motion Lab). It follows the phone’s reduce-motion setting until you pick one; Off skips the opening film.

60.title: Dad test
60.desc: Dropped (you, Oct 20: "Too focused on my dad's easy navigation ... Just make my experience and he will check it and be like damn nice"). The app is designed for your own experience; no separate Dad test.

61.title: Phase 2 photo standard and a 5-coin test shoot
61.desc: Light, background, scale and file names for the pro photos, tested on 5 coins end to end before the real run (pairing, 2×2 and circle crops, registering, the quality check), so 290 coins are shot once. The scan page's photo checks (#65) are the start of the quality gate.
61.needs: nothing for the test; the full shoot needs #5

62.title: Real collector values
62.desc: Two paths, both built: Grok has appraiser homework (each value citing the exact price page and the grade assumed; a cited value is re-appraised after a year), and a weekly GitHub job fetches Numista's price estimates per grade once you add a free Numista API key. Oct 14: Grok and Gemini priced 63 of the same coins independently and agreed on 62. Values still change only through a cited file.
62.needs: your free Numista API key (Waiting on you)

63.title: Motion into the app
63.desc: Started (tr108-tr110): the 20 animation styles now run inside the themes and every theme opens with its own motion splash (#110, #112). Still to come: only the Motion Lab studies you pick from #56 (coin flip, tile to coin view, Confirm seal, album settle), calm by default and off when the phone asks for less motion.
63.needs: your picks from #56 (the motion setting #59 is done)

64.title: Printable inventory for insurance and family
64.desc: Oct 9 (tr105): rebuilt on every update, linked from Health: an insurance copy (with values and how sure we are) and a family copy without values. Photo, id, what it is, where it came from, a tick-off column; prints on Letter or A4. Still yours to decide: which copy goes to whom.
64.needs: the missing photos (shoot list); better with #62

65.title: Scan a coin in the app
65.desc: Version 1 is live: Hall footer → Scan a coin (or Lab → Shoot list → Scan with the camera). Pick the coin (your shoot list first), take the photo, see whether it is sharp, big enough and free of glare, and send it to Drive STAGING or to an AI app with the reading prompt, already named the way the pipeline expects. Next: the AI that wins the locked test (#19) reads it without leaving the app (needs a key that never sits in the public site).

66.title: Deep review by four outside AIs
66.desc: Oct 8 (tr99): Grok, Muse, ChatGPT and Gemini each reviewed the whole project; every claim was checked against the files before anything was used. Scores: Grok 10, Muse 8, ChatGPT 5 (it read an old copy), Gemini 1 (it could not open the files and invented a review). 43 coin corrections merged: Vietnam, Greece, Malta, Netherlands, Philippines, UK mintages, East Caribbean, Saudi, Cuba, Thailand, the Swiss 2 francs split, the Greek coin's story.

67.title: The whole collection works offline
67.desc: Every coin's page, search and the questions are now saved on the phone after the app opens, not only the Hall; Health has “Save all coin photos for offline”. The smoke test proves it by opening a never-viewed coin with the network off.

68.title: The big number moves with silver and gold
68.desc: The headline used to be the Sept 30 figure ($5,369). It now uses the latest daily metal prices and says which day, the same number as the Portfolio chart.

69.title: Truth checks on every publish
69.desc: A new check finds records that contradict each other or claim more than their evidence (Health → Contradictions to check). It went from 257 findings to 31: 114 mintages given their one home, 111 stale “unknown” notes cleared. What is left is real work: the Swiss 1968 conflict (#71), the C238 portrait, and 28 US/German coins whose mint letter can't be read.

70.title: Contract holes closed
70.desc: Every AI catalogue fact now needs the exact entry or the photo, even when the source names no site; the Oct 21 provenance deadline goes by the day of the merge, not the AI's own clock; a coin's mintage has one home and writing it on one coin updates the others of that issue; publishing can no longer leave the app half-written.

71.title: Settle the Swiss 1968 B mintage
71.desc: Oct 8 (tr102): Grok read the 1968 B row of Numista N#189: 31,588,000 struck at Bern; the 10,000,000 is London’s 1968 striking without a mint mark. Both coins now show 31,588,000 (labelled Reference).

72.title: Grok's Numista sweep (round 1)
72.desc: Oct 8 (tr102): Grok swept 152 of 162 types in 9 batches overnight: 484 facts, each with the exact Numista entry and the row it read. Catalogue fixes (Guatemala, Trinidad, Mexico, Vietnam, Jamaica, USSR), catalogue weights and sizes instead of ranges, Schön numbers. The trust meter went from 5.7 % to 18.1 %. Round 2 (47 types, 93 facts and 31 catalogue numbers) is in its queue.

73.title: Fact-check the stories
73.desc: Part of the research loop: every story nobody but its author has checked is a job. Grok's checks so far all held up; it has C151-C283 plus 33 more stories as homework. A checked story is re-sent with the exact entry it was checked against; a wrong sentence is corrected with its source.

74.title: Source chips that open the exact entry
74.desc: Oct 9 (tr104): tap any label in a coin's view: the panel now has “Open the source” links to the exact entry (Numista N#… opens its catalogue page), so a right number on the wrong coin shows at a glance.

75.title: One honest trust meter
75.desc: Oct 8 (tr100): the Hall, the Simple view and Health show how much of what the app says is proven: today 5.7 % of the 3,181 facts on screen are cited or confirmed (69 % come from the original ledger unchecked, 21 % are AI readings, 2.5 % read from a photo). It rises every time you confirm a fact or an AI cites the exact entry.

76.title: A change log that can never be quietly rewritten
76.desc: Oct 9 (tr104): every line of the change history is chained to the one before (collection/changes.chain). Saving refuses to change an old line, the checker compares the chain with the file, and a GitHub job checks on every update that the history only grew. The fingerprint is published with the data, so any saved copy pins the history up to its day.

77.title: Where each coin came from
77.desc: Ready: Questions → “Where did they come from?”: pick how (bought, inherited, a gift, found, a trip), from whom and when, tick the coins by country, send. They become your own records and show in each coin's view and the printable inventory.

78.title: Confirm while you hold it
78.desc: Oct 8 (tr100): every coin on the shoot list shows up to 3 facts to check in hand (“Right? Year 1978”). One tap queues the confirmation for the Questions page; your answers file turns them into verified facts.

79.title: Fingerprint every photo
79.desc: Oct 9 (tr104): all 217 cut-outs carry the fingerprint of the original phone photo they were cut from, checked against Drive by file id (13 same-name duplicates caught). A photo without one is flagged in Health.

80.title: Dad-facing fixes from the reviews
80.desc: A tap anywhere now skips the opening film (it used to turn the sound on); Skip is large and readable over any frame; Simple view labels follow its 22 px base (some were 13–16 px); Questions says “can't load” when offline instead of “no open questions”.

81.title: Haptics on phones
81.desc: Oct 8 (tr100): a tiny tick when you tap a button, tab or chip; a double tick for a confirm or an answer. Android vibrates; iPhone (iOS 18) gets the system tick. Switch: next to Motion in Settings.

82.title: Sound: smooth start, on by default, one tap = the whole scene
82.desc: Oct 8 (tr101): the stutter at the start came from work piling up in the first two seconds (measuring loudness on the phone, building the reverb, switching the effect, a fragile background-sound route). All moved out of the way: start-up blocking went from about 1.2 s to 0.1 s on a fast computer. Sound now starts with your first tap (Off is remembered). Tapping a theme brings its sound and music; tapping a scene brings its lighting and effect.

83.title: Real classical recordings
83.desc: 23 recordings play now, in the scenes and on the radio's Classical station. Oct 9: Handel's Largo (Ombra mai fu) is live, sung by Lea Desandre with Les Arts Florissants (CC BY 3.0), so the 1920 Caruso question is gone; every file was re-made at the intended 96 kb/s, so most got smaller. Still nothing qualifying for Nimrod, Rêverie or a piano Gymnopédie No. 3: they are re-searched on every music run, and Grok has them as a project.

84.title: Always work queued for the other AIs
84.desc: Oct 8: Grok, Muse and ChatGPT each have a standing queue (Gemini’s is parked until you fix it): Drive “WORK QUEUE for …” docs, and a GitHub page for ChatGPT. Each starts the next task by itself; I refresh the queues at every intake. See “The other AIs” above.

85.title: The research loop: homework generated from the data
85.desc: Oct 9 (tr104): every gap in the data is a job (cite a catalogue fact, check another AI's fact, read a mint mark, fact-check or simplify a story, answer a research question, appraise a value, settle a disagreement). After every update the loop closes answered homework, hands each AI new assignments in the kinds it is best at, never its own facts, and measures how often each one is wrong. docs/agents/RESEARCH_LOOP.md.

86.title: “Checked”: two independent sources agree
86.desc: Oct 9 (tr104): a new label above Reference. A fact is Checked when two different contributors each stated it with their own exact source or photo; an AI never checks itself. 25 facts so far; every check another AI does adds more.

87.title: Answer sheets and a gate that never overwrites
87.desc: Oct 9 (tr104): every assignment comes with a pre-filled answer sheet; an unfilled line is simply left out, a line written against an old value is skipped (not a rejected file), and a check that disagrees is filed, never written over the record. A mintage or catalogue number is never accepted on a photo alone.

88.title: The blind photo tests recur by themselves
88.desc: Oct 9 (tr105): each AI is due the main test every 6 months and the locked test every 90 days; due tests appear at the top of its page and the scores are logged, so accuracy is measured over time, not once.

89.title: A coin's year list can no longer shift under pending files
89.desc: Oct 9 (tr104): adding a new coin used to re-sort its type's years, so an AI line written for “the 4th year” could land on another year with the same empty value. Years are now append-only.

90.title: Held music is searched again on every run
90.desc: Oct 9: pieces with no qualifying recording are re-searched on every music run and reported, never used until reviewed. It found Handel's Ombra mai fu by Les Arts Florissants on its first run. Also fixed: the encoder had silently lost its quality settings.

91.title: Scores drafted by the pipeline
91.desc: Each submission's score (right place, accepted as sent, accurate, complete, in its tier) drafted from the merge report and the cross-checks, so CONTRIBUTOR_SCORES and each AI's feedback stay current without my bookkeeping; I only adjust and add the praise.

92.title: The loop turns without a chat: autonomous intake
92.desc: Built and tested (tr107). Every hour a GitHub job asks a small Google Apps Script in your Drive for new change files, merges the outside AIs' files through every gate and test, publishes, turns the loop and rebuilds the site; the Drive side then trashes merged files, leaves REJECTED notes with a HOW TO FIX line and refreshes each AI's WORK QUEUE doc. Owner answers and anything that needs judgement wait for me in docs/agents/bridge/INBOX.md. No GitHub key anywhere: the job uses GitHub's own short-lived token.
92.needs: you: the one-time install, about 10 minutes (docs/INTAKE_BRIDGE.md: one Apps Script project, two GitHub secrets)
92.unlocks: #50, #93, daily progress with no session open
92.note: Off until the install; the hourly job checks for the two secrets and does nothing without them.

93.title: Each AI's page copied to its Drive doc automatically
93.desc: Built (tr116): the loop now writes each AI's compact Drive copy (docs/agents/drive/QUEUE_{ai}.txt: its NEW note, the live link, one line per assignment), and the Drive bridge copies that file into the AI's doc whenever it changes. Until the bridge is installed I paste the same file by hand.

94.title: Old sources re-checked on a cadence
94.desc: Oct 15 (tr116): each month a sample of 12 Checked facts cited more than a year ago goes back to a second reader (never to either of the two who checked it); a changed entry becomes a disagreement. Nothing is that old yet, so the first ones come in October 2027.

95.title: My own spot checks counted
95.desc: Oct 15 (tr116): my own spot checks at an intake go through the same gate as an AI's check (workflow spot-check): the same value with my source = Checked and counted as a check I did; a different value = a disagreement for a third reader, never an overwrite.

96.title: Cost per checked fact
96.desc: Oct 15 (tr116): collaborators/AI_RUNS.md now shows, per AI, how many of its facts another contributor checked, how many held up, how many were wrong, and the cost per fact that held up (when the AI reports its cost).

97.title: One onboarding path for any new AI
97.desc: Oct 15 (tr116): one path, written down (RESEARCH_LOOP.md section 9) and one command (tools/agents/new_agent.py): proof of access, the main photo test, half batches with every fact checked, full batches after the first good submission, off probation after 3 in a row that score 8+.

98.title: Targets and progress per kind of fact
98.desc: Goals like every catalogue number Checked by January, every mint mark read by Phase 2, every story checked by someone other than its author, with a progress line for each in Health.

99.title: Canary checks for the checkers
99.desc: Oct 15 (tr116): about 6 % of the values a check list shows are planted wrong on purpose (a real value of the same field from another coin type; the record stays right). An AI that sends one back unchanged was rubber-stamping; one that sends the true value caught it. Never filed as a disagreement; counted on the AI's page and in metrics (tools/pipeline/canary.py).

100.title: Re-test an AI when its model changes
100.desc: Oct 15 (tr116): a model name never seen before for an AI (provenance.model in its files) makes it new again: for 30 days its facts are checked first, and both photo tests come back on its page. Gemini coming back on Argon is the first case.

101.title: A third research AI, so disagreements never wait on me
101.desc: Oct 15 (tr116): Gemini is back on every surface (Argon chat, Antigravity, Spark; owner: "I pay for the shit so I expect it to function as we desire"), with arbitration first on its list, so Grok-vs-Muse disagreements no longer wait for me.

102.title: Every contradiction becomes homework
102.desc: Oct 15 (tr116): a new homework kind, contradictions: every truth-check finding that needs research (30 today: German and US coins with a mintage but no mint mark read) goes to an AI as a job with an exact ask; the mechanical ones are still fixed by the script. Grok and Gemini have the first batches.

103.title: Warn when the Drive backup is stale
103.desc: Health shows the age of the newest Drive backup and warns past 7 days. Today the only Drive copy is from Sept 28.
103.needs: the Drive backup installed (it comes with the #92 install)

104.title: Export everything in plain formats
104.desc: Oct 20: data/export/ is rebuilt on every publish: coins.csv (all 306 pieces, 41 columns, with "how sure" and the source for 9 key facts), album_holes.csv (all 1,775 holes, with the price and source of each missing one), lots.csv, collection.json (the whole master record plus every certainty label) and a plain README. Opens in Excel, Numbers or Google Sheets; linked from the printable inventory (insurance copy).

105.title: A recovery card
105.desc: Oct 20: written. Repo copy docs/RECOVERY_CARD.md; Drive doc 'RECOVERY CARD (print this, keep it in the safe)' in Titan Reliquary/: where everything lives, which accounts own it, what to do if the site stops loading or GitHub is gone (rebuild from the backup zip in plain steps), and where the spreadsheet export is. Your part: print it, write the GitHub and Google recovery codes on it by hand, put it in the safe.

106.title: Who can change what
106.desc: Oct 20: docs/WHO_CAN_CHANGE_WHAT.md lists every way in (GitHub accounts and app, each GitHub job's token, the repo secrets, Drive and its connectors, the Apps Script) with its guard. Narrowed: the integrity, smoke and restore-drill jobs now get read-only tokens. Two paths are wider than needed and wait for you: #127.

107.title: What completing each album would cost
107.desc: Started (tr114): What's missing and the Simple view now show a price on every missing hole of albums A001-A016 and a cost to complete per album (Grok's list from price guides: 289 holes, about $2,731 in all). It is a floor: key dates look low against dealer guides, so Grok is getting a second source for the 10 most expensive holes. Muse has A017-A033. HOLD stays the policy; this is for planning and wish lists.
107.needs: Muse's prices for A017-A033; Grok's second source

108.title: Family stories for each coin
108.desc: Your words (or your dad's) about a coin: who had it, where it was found. Typed or a voice note turned into text, kept as the owner's own story, which always wins over an AI's.

109.title: Your dad's phone
109.desc: Dropped with #60 (Oct 20): your dad uses the same app as you.

110.title: The 20 animation styles, inside the themes
110.desc: Done (tr108-tr110), from your first video: every one of the 20 styles is a live GPU effect in the theme it suits: Particles in Midnight Gallery, Liquid morph in The Mint, Holographic in Prism, Neon glow + Retro VHS in Neon Vault, Wireframe 3D in Solar Observatory, Glassmorphism in Hyperborean Vault, ASCII art in The Construct, Gradient mesh in Samadhi, Art deco in Nocturne, Halftone in Conservator, Neo-brutalism in Plaintext; the other nine got new themes (#111). Each theme's old signature effect stays underneath, softer, and each has a rare “moment” with a sound (#21). Every theme passes the contrast check.

111.title: Six new themes for the styles that had no home
111.desc: Done (tr108): Arcade (pixel art), Pulp Adventure (comic book), Drafting Room (blueprint), Clay Diorama (clay 3D + isometric), Bauhaus (Bauhaus + kinetic type) and Grand Terminal (split-flap departures board with your 50 countries). 26 themes now, in a new “Studio” group; each has its own colours, crest, sound scene and interface touches (ink outlines, pixel corners, blueprint lines...). The Themes picker now shows every theme with a small live preview.

112.title: A motion splash for every theme
112.desc: Done (tr110-tr113): each of the 26 themes has its own 3-second motion in its style (dust forming the title, molten letters, a KAPOW, a split-flap board, a coin drawn as a blueprint...). Since tr112 every launch plays the Grok film, then the theme's motion, then the app (a tap skips to the app); since tr113 picking a theme plays its motion too. Scene Studio > Settings > Opening changes it; Calm shows one still frame; Off skips it.

113.title: Pictures for every theme card
113.desc: Mostly done (tr114): Grok made picker cards for all 26 themes; 25 are live (Midnight Gallery keeps its own), and themes without a wide picture use the card. Still open: the 22 wide heroes (Muse) and refreshed heroes for Prism, Midnight Gallery, The Mint and Shipwreck (Gemini, when it is back).

114.title: Try the new effects on your phone
114.desc: Every effect and splash was tuned on a software graphics chip in my container, never on a real phone. Open a few themes on yours and tell me which effects are too strong, too faint or stutter; I tune them in one pass.

115.title: Effects keep moving while you scroll
115.desc: Done (tr111): since tr82 the effects froze while a page scrolled (to keep scrolling smooth on phones). Now they keep moving at a scroll frame rate that steps down from 30 to 20 to 12 frames a second if the phone struggles, never to zero, and the text protection follows the page as it moves.

116.title: Rethink the interface beyond the wings (AI homework)
116.desc: Oct 15: your call ("the framework is good but the UI still sucks... too fixed into the wings... more novel ways of presenting data"). A design brief (docs/design/REDESIGN_BRIEF.md, also in Drive 'design-incoming (AI UI proposals)') lists every function to keep, what is wrong today, the bar and the hard rules. Grok proposes a structure beyond the five wings with a working prototype, Gemini builds two prototypes (a novel data view and the atmosphere control), Muse walks the app on a phone and ranks what is clunky with ten references. I host the good prototypes side by side at /prototypes/v2/ for you to try; only what you pick goes into the app, in small steps. Oct 16: Grok's The Field is hosted at /prototypes/v2/grok/ (v2 sent, see #123); Gemini's Continuum v2 scored 3/10 blind, every one of its 12 ideas kept, and became Titan v3 (#119-#121).

117.title: A better atmosphere control (replaces the Scene Studio panel)
117.desc: You called it clunky: themes, sound, effects and settings are one long panel. Gemini prototypes one smooth control with a live preview (part of #116); the winner replaces the panel, keeping every setting. Oct 16: now part of Titan v3 step 3 (#121).

118.title: Answers you send get a receipt
118.desc: Done (tr116; you: "How do I know that you got those three answers?"). Questions has Send to Claude: it opens GitHub with your answers filled in, you press Submit, and a robot (owner-answers.yml, only for your own issues) merges them, publishes and replies on the issue. The phone shows each batch as Not sent, Sent (waiting) or Received with the counts, whichever way you sent it (GitHub, a chat copy or a Drive file). Offline it says so and keeps them.

119.title: Titan v3, step 1: the whole collection as one 3D space, and one coin
119.desc: All 306 pieces as real 3D coins with their phone photos; filters and sorts move the coins instead of redrawing a list; tap a coin and it flies forward into its own view (flip, a raking light you drag, a loupe, every fact with its certainty label), back flies it home; search moves the camera. Gemini's plan for it is accepted as the spec (docs/design/v3/M1_SPEC.md, Oct 16); the build itself has not arrived yet. I check Drive for it on Oct 17 (16:30 UTC); if it is still missing I ask you whether I should build it from the spec. On hold (you, Oct 20): wait while Grok upgrades the themes on main.

120.title: Titan v3, step 2: albums as real pages
120.desc: Each album as a physical page with real holes: filled holes hold the coin, missing ones are empty and lit, printed circles look different, pages turn. "Which Silver Eagle year am I missing?" answered in a couple of taps from opening, in the main app. Cost to complete and the want list from data/wants.json.

121.title: Titan v3, step 3: live value and three showpiece worlds
121.desc: The headline value moves with the metal prices; one world switch changes look, light, effect and sound together as a transition instead of a settings panel (this replaces #117). Three worlds made at showpiece quality instead of 26, each with its own badge drawn from scratch: on Oct 16 you judged all 23 badge pairs and 5 theme pairs "both weak", ours as well as Gemini's.

122.title: Judge every design blind before it ships
122.desc: Started Oct 16: the blind review page showed each badge and theme as A and B in random order and saved your picks (claude.ai/artifact/5bc8r7rf9Urx4QEdr8at1K). It found that Gemini's 24 theme files were our files with 187 lines changed (19 look identical on screen) and that all 28 pairs were "both weak". Every Titan v3 step, Grok's The Field and any new theme goes through the same test against today's app before anything changes in the app.

123.title: Process Grok's Oct 16 drop
123.desc: Oct 20: Grok's Oct 15-19 files and Muse's Oct 17 files merged through the gates (175 lines), the C301 and C304 photos cut and live, 37 disagreements settled (Grok won every one Claude could decide, incl. the euro globe/map side on 10 types). Scores: Grok 9, Muse 7. The Field v2 was already hosted by Grok at /prototypes/v2/grok/.

124.title: Decide on two possible duplicates: C300 and C301
124.desc: Oct 19 (you): keep both. C301 has its own photo now (Oct 20: the file filed under C293 was really C301's 1989 coin, so that photo is retired); C293 and C300 still need a photo of their own (shoot list).

125.title: Check the ledger's facts against the photos
125.desc: Oct 20: 1,106 facts on screen still come straight from Grok's original ledger, never checked, and the first 3 ever checked were all wrong. The year, mint and face value of every coin with a photo (441 facts) now go to the AIs first as blind photo reads; a second agreeing read makes a fact Checked. Batches are bigger too (Grok 24 assignments, Muse 20, Gemini 16; about 900 items out today).

126.title: A varieties checklist for the pro-photo session
126.desc: Grok's new homework: for every US, UK and German coin in a flip, the known varieties and errors of that exact year and mint (small/large date, doubled dies, wide/close AM...), what to look for under the loupe, on which side, and what it is worth if found. Becomes the Phase 2 shoot checklist, so no variety is missed while the coin is out of its flip.

127.title: Narrow two write paths (your call)
127.desc: From the #106 review. (1) Since Oct 19 grok-bot pushes code straight to main; the checks run after, but nothing stops a bad push. Safer: Grok pushes to grok/* branches and I merge as soon as integrity and smoke are green. (2) Grok, Muse and Gemini reach your whole Google Drive through their connections. Narrower: a separate Google account that only holds the shared Titan Reliquary folder. Say yes to either and I write Grok's new instructions or the share steps.
